transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. As we all know, the new event-ingestion service is scheduled to enter production next Monday. Before we can finalize the design, I need to go through our standard sign-off checklist. I'd like to hear from backend engineering, infrastructure, customer success operations, and security — in that order — on any blockers or required controls you see with the current draft design, which proposes active-active replication, a 90-day event-retention period, and an initial limit of 96 partitions. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker. While reviewing an unrelated consumer integration this morning, I confirmed that the existing Ledger event consumer cannot preserve ordering across active-active replication. Production compatibility requires active-passive replication plus an explicit per-aggregate ordering guardrail. I have not yet updated the architecture document, but this directly conflicts with the active-active replication proposed in the draft design.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a blocker on the partition count. I confirmed from the current production load model just ten minutes ago that the shared cluster can only support at most 48 partitions for this service without starving the checkout stream — not the 96 proposed in the draft. I was still reconciling the capacity worksheet and hadn't posted the number yet, but this needs to be factored into the sign-off decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a blocker from customer success operations. In a contract review this afternoon, I found that the enterprise tenant Linden requires all event processing and storage to remain in the EU region — no cross-region replication is permitted for their data. Linden is included in the proposed initial cohort, and I have not yet added the required EU-only routing exception to the design ticket. This conflicts with the active-active replication in the draft design, which would replicate Linden's events across regions.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a security blocker. During a separate token-hardening task today, my security scan found personal data in the event payloads. This means the service requires field-level encryption and a maximum 30-day retention period — the proposed 90-day retention would violate our data protection requirements. I have not yet opened the security finding, but this needs to be addressed before production sign-off.
